earlier_scan.source_named: Tosco, Mauro 1989. Schizzo grammaticale del dialetto Karre di Qoryooley (grammar sketch named on Glottolog; not found online)

new_statements.quote: Come negli altri dialetti somali, accento e tono in K. coincidono, nel senso che la mora — e non la sillaba — cui è assegnato l'accento di parola, viene realizzata con un tono alto (´). Ogni parola può avere un solo tono alto. Come in Maay, la maggior parte dei nomi — sia maschili che femminili — hanno un tono alto sull'ultima mora: (24) ukúr (m.) "ombelico" / babáʔ (f.) "palmo della mano" / habár (f.) "donna" / webí (m.) "fiume" [p. 24:] Molti bisillabi, sia maschili che femminili, hanno invece un tono alto sulla prima mora: (25) bábbas (m.) "cenere" (T.) / támmar (m.) "colostro" / úsbu (m.) "sale" / kárab (m.) "spalla; ala" ...
new_statements.translation: As in the other Somali dialects, accent and tone coincide in K[arre], in the sense that the mora — not the syllable — to which word accent is assigned is realized with a high tone (´). Each word can have only one high tone. As in Maay, most nouns — both masculine and feminine — have a high tone on the last mora: (24) ukúr (m.) 'navel', babáʔ (f.) 'palm of the hand', habár (f.) 'woman', webí (m.) 'river'. [p. 24:] Many disyllables, both masculine and feminine, instead have a high tone on the first mora: (25) bábbas (m.) 'ash' (Tuuf), támmar (m.) 'colostrum', úsbu (m.) 'salt', kárab (m.) 'shoulder; wing' ...
new_statements.citation: Tosco, Mauro. 1989. Schizzo grammaticale del dialetto Karre di Qoryooley. Studi Somali 9. Roma: Ministero degli Affari Esteri, Dipartimento per la Cooperazione allo Sviluppo, Comitato Tecnico Linguistico per l'Università Nazionale Somala.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (161 pp., scanned, no text layer; extracted text on the two pages returns 2 bytes;..). Rendered PDF pp. 22-24 (printed pp. 23-25) and pp. 1, 5-6 and read the page images directly. Printed p. 23 carries the headings "1.4. Accento, tono e intonazione" and "1.4.1. Accento e tono" and the sentences "Come negli altri dialetti somali, accento e tono in K. coincidono, nel senso che la mora — e non la sillaba — cui è assegnato l'accento di parola, viene realizzata con un tono alto (´). Ogni parola può avere un solo tono alto. Come in Maay, la maggior parte dei nomi — sia maschili che femminili — hanno un tono alto sull'ultima mora: (24) ukúr (m.) 'ombelico', babáʔ (f.) 'palmo della mano', ha…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Somali-type tonal accent: one accented mora per word, realized as a single high tone; placement is not fixed. Nouns: the majority carry the high tone on the final mora, but many disyllabic nouns carry it on the first mora; short-vowel monosyllables are high if masculine and low if feminine; long-vowel monosyllables have the high tone on the first mora (i.e. falling). Verbs: the present/future positive endings carry the high tone; in the past the high tone falls on the first mora of the stem (except 2Pl/3Pl, high on the ending); imperative has the high tone on the last mora in the singular and on the penult in the plural; jussive -o endings are high; the invariable negative has stem-high.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned; the source states each word can have only one high tone ('Ogni parola può avere un solo tono alto').
new_statements.exceptions: Nouns split between final-mora (majority) and first-mora (many disyllables) high tone; monosyllable tone depends on gender and vowel length; verb tone is set by tense/mood/person (p. 24). Tosco warns (p. 23) that the analysis is 'del tutto iniziale', a set of preliminary notes that further research could substantially change; nothing can be said about tonal case marking on nouns or main-vs-dependent verb tone, and verb tone patterns seem sensitive to sentence intonation and possibly clause type (p. 24).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, isolated words in a fieldwork corpus from the Tuuf-lineage Karre of Qoryooley; the author says the relation between word tone and phrase intonation remains to be investigated (p. 23). §1.4.2 (p. 25) covers only sentence intonation (general pitch raising in yes/no questions, no final intensity drop).
new_statements.identity_note: Tosco 1989 describes the Karre (= Garre) spoken in the district of Qoryooley, Lower Shabelle, Somalia, specifically the Tuuf lineage ('Garre qofar'), with occasional Qurapow notes (pp. 5-6). It is the same variety Glottolog files as garr1259 / ISO gex (Somalia). Tosco stresses that the Garre of Mandera/Moyale (Kenya, Ethiopia; 'Garre libin') speak essentially a Borana (Oromo) dialect, and Lamberti reports that Garre of Baydhaba differs (loss of prefix conjugation); the statement therefore applies to the Qoryooley/Lower Shabelle variety, not to Kenyan 'Garre'.

sources.note: §1.4 'Accento, tono e intonazione' (pp. 23-25): accent and tone coincide as in other Somali dialects; the accented MORA (not syllable) carries one high tone per word; most nouns (m. and f.) have H on the last mora, many disyllables on the first mora; short-vowel monosyllables H if masculine, L if feminine; long-vowel monosyllables H on first mora; verb tone is morphologically determined (present/future endings H; past H on first mora of stem except 2Pl/3Pl; imperative sg final, pl penult). Author flags the analysis as preliminary.
